adoption.scope: Lv1-Lv60 progression, character currencies, Huaguoshan reward profiles and pity, public participation chest P1, Tongtian Tower first-cycle rewards, and persistent receipt semantics.
adoption.implementation_boundary: This is an accepted design resource table. It must not be copied into implementation/growth, Y3, an object editor, a ledger store, or a live service until a separately reviewed runtime integration consumes it.
adoption.immutable_change_rule: Any numerical, qualification, reward, pity, or receipt change creates a new resource_table_version and may never recalculate an existing receipt.

progression.future_source_profile_mapping_boundary: The Lv21-Lv60 curve and source-kind budget are frozen, but no Difu or TianTing encounter may grant XP until a separately versioned chapter source-profile allocation table maps its authoritative source_profile, count, and rounding to this budget. An unmapped encounter must not infer an XP grant.

party_policy.death_rule: A dead character receives no new live-combat XP; an already committed receipt remains replayable after revive.
party_policy.reconnect_rule: Reconnect reconciles the original receipt and must retain the original authoritative xp_session_id; it cannot issue a new XP grant or open a new repeat-clear quota.
party_policy.repeat_clear_rule: A repeat clear uses repeat multiplier 2500 basis points against its configured first-clear XP, rounds down before the over-level multiplier, and may settle at most once for the same owner_id, xp_source_key, and xp_session_id. Tower grants no XP.

repeat_clear_quota.session_lifecycle: xp_session_id is created only by the authoritative session-open transition and ends only at the authoritative session-close transition. Reconnect, a new encounter_instance_id, a new event_id, party reshaping, or a client retry must retain the same xp_session_id; only a later authoritative session-open after close may create a new value.
repeat_clear_quota.quota_consume_rule: A committed repeat XP receipt consumes exactly one quota entry. Rejected, cap-blocked, duplicate, and unresolved prepared receipts do not consume it. The quota lookup and receipt commit use the same compare-and-swap or serializable transaction.

xp_receipt_calculation.formula: repeat_adjusted_xp = floor(xp_base_amount * xp_repeat_multiplier_basis_points / 10000); experience_delta = floor(repeat_adjusted_xp * xp_over_level_multiplier_basis_points / 10000)
xp_receipt_calculation.level_cap_rule: At Lv60 a new experience settlement is rejected with experience_delta=0 and award_outcome=rejected; it must not consume a repeat quota.

balance_and_stack_cap_policy.overflow_outcome: commit a zero-award receipt with award_outcome=balance_or_stack_cap_reached; do not consume a first-clear entitlement, grant a partial award, or advance pity. When pity_pool_key is non-null, the receipt must record pity_before and pity_after as equal values.

forbidden_value_paths: No currency, material, rare eligibility, pity progress, experience multiplier, or tower entry may be sold or accelerated by payment.
Materials remain item records and may not be represented as a second currency ledger.
A missing configured sink rejects the spend; it may not silently consume or mint a balance.

qualification.progression_participation: damage_ratio_ge_0.03 OR valid_break OR valid_guard OR one_valid_public_action
qualification.participation_chest_eligibility: when a qualifying public-action window opened: valid_public_action AND (damage_ratio_ge_0.03 OR valid_break OR valid_guard); otherwise: damage_ratio_ge_0.03 OR valid_break OR valid_guard
qualification.public_rare_eligibility: For public_rare_drop only: authority_attested_rare_clear AND (damage_ratio_ge_0.03 OR valid_break OR valid_guard); a rare roll additionally requires a settled eligible participation-chest receipt but is never inferred from that chest result

public_chest_settlement.source_profile_rule: source_profile equals the exact public profile_key; the policy ID is carried separately in p1_policy_id.
public_chest_settlement.content_rule: A committed eligible participation_chest is the only base-bundle grant for its public profile and awards that profile's public_boss bundle. The same public event must not also create a drop_bundle receipt.
public_chest_settlement.downstream_binding_rule: A public first_clear_grant or public_rare_drop must bind the committed eligible participation_chest receipt with the same owner_id, event_id, encounter_instance_id, qualification_snapshot_id, source_profile, and resource_table_version.

team_raid_policy.participation: joined_before_lock AND present_at_completion AND actor_alive_at_completion AND contribution_attested
team_raid_policy.public_participation_chest_precondition: not-applicable; team_raid_rare_drop binds only the TEAM_RAID_RARE_ELIGIBILITY_V1 snapshot and authority proof
team_raid_policy.receipt_identity_binding: For team_raid_rare_drop, receipt.event_id MUST equal completion_event_id, receipt.encounter_instance_id MUST equal raid_instance_id, and source_profile MUST equal the exact eligible team-raid profile_key.

pity_pools.increment_after: an eligible rare roll misses and its receipt commits
pity_pools.reset_after: a rare success, a pity-forced success, or a duplicate conversion from that rare success
pity_pools.migration: carry only through an explicit same-family migration record

pity_pools.increment_after: an eligible rare roll misses and its receipt commits
pity_pools.reset_after: a rare success, a pity-forced success, or a duplicate conversion from that rare success
pity_pools.migration: carry only through an explicit same-family migration record

profile_settlement_contract.settlement_trigger: one authoritative completion or clear event per source_profile and encounter_instance_id
profile_settlement_contract.repeat_rule: A profile may pay again only for a new authoritative event_id. The same source_profile and event_id in the same encounter_instance_id replay the original receipt and may never reissue a grant.
profile_settlement_contract.first_clear_version_rule: A later resource_table_version never resets an existing first-clear history key; any duplicate conversion uses the profile rule preserved on the original receipt.
profile_settlement_contract.pity_increment_boundary: Only a committed eligible rare miss advances a listed pity pool; ordinary bundle settlement, qualification failure, cap failure, and rejected receipts do not.

drops_and_pity.profile_boundary: Profiles without a rare field are deterministic guaranteed bundles plus their stated first-clear rule; they must not acquire a hidden probability, pity pool, or duplicate conversion.

tower_rewards.entry_rule: every solo player or every member of a team must be at least Lv55
tower_rewards.cooperative_rule: A team completion produces one individually qualified receipt only for a member that passes TOWER_FIRST_CYCLE_QUALIFICATION_V1; no pooled currency or team wallet exists.

qualification_policy.eligibility: entry_level_at_least_55 AND entry_qualified AND joined_before_run_lock AND present_at_authoritative_completion AND actor_alive_at_authoritative_completion AND contribution_attested
qualification_policy.receipt_binding: For tower_reward, receipt.owner_id must name an eligible snapshot member, receipt.event_id must equal completion_event_id, and receipt tower_run_id/tower_cycle_id/tower_week_bucket/tower_mode must equal that snapshot. A disconnected, absent, dead, non-contributing, late-joining, or entry-ineligible member receives no tower_reward receipt.

tower_rewards.first_clear_version_rule: A later resource_table_version never resets a tower first-clear history key.

weekly_cap_policy.bucket: Asia/Shanghai ISO-8601 week derived by the authoritative service clock
weekly_cap_policy.cap_reached_outcome: commit a zero-award receipt with award_outcome=weekly_token_cap_reached; do not consume the first-clear entitlement, grant materials, or advance any pity state. tower_weekly_token_before and tower_weekly_token_after must be equal.
weekly_cap_policy.concurrency_rule: Read the weekly issued-token counter, verify planned_tokens <= cap - tower_weekly_token_before, write tower_weekly_token_after, the first-clear state, receipt origin, and receipt commit in one serializable transaction or compare-and-swap guarded transaction. A competing settlement re-reads the committed counter before it can award.

tower_mode_contract.alias_policy: mode is forbidden; no case, whitespace, or semantic alias is accepted.

tower_rewards.global_tower_boundary: Floor plan, affix pool, total floors, season, title asset IDs, cosmetic asset IDs, and exchange catalog remain separate content/runtime decisions. This reward table rejects settlement if tower_run_id or tower_cycle_id is absent.

canonical_receipt_field_contract.comparison: All canonical values are exact, case-sensitive ASCII identifiers. Whitespace, case, legacy aliases, display names, and inferred defaults are forbidden.

transactional_resolution_contract.lock_and_plan: For a new semantic identity, one serializable transaction first acquires the unique receipt identity and every affected first-clear, pity, XP repeat-quota, tower weekly-quota, balance, and stack lock; only after those locks are held may it resolve the complete final award plan, including zero-award cap outcomes and counter before/after values.
transactional_resolution_contract.commit: The same transaction writes every reward/state mutation, origin, and one terminal committed receipt with the resolved award_plan_hash. A rejected receipt is terminal and writes no reward, pity, first-clear, repeat quota, weekly quota, or origin mutation.
transactional_resolution_contract.retry: An aborted transaction leaves no durable receipt or mutation. A retry may use only the same immutable authoritative inputs (including event identity, qualification snapshot, drop_roll_id, and XP inputs); it reacquires locks before resolving a new terminal plan. Once a terminal receipt exists, it always replays; a different fingerprint is receipt_identity_conflict.

persistent_receipt_contract.profile_scope_receipt_rule: For drop_bundle and first_clear_grant, source_profile equals an exact profile_key. drop_bundle excludes all public profiles because their base bundle is paid by participation_chest. team_raid profiles require a non-null qualification_snapshot_id from TEAM_RAID_RARE_ELIGIBILITY_V1; ordinary encounter profiles keep it null. first_clear_disposition is first_clear_granted, duplicate_conversion, or not_consumed_zero_award, and only first_clear_grant may set it non-null.
persistent_receipt_contract.public_chest_profile_binding_rule: participation_chest requires p1_policy_id=P1_PUBLIC_CHEST_BALANCED_CONTRIBUTION and one allowed public source_profile. For a public source_profile, first_clear_grant and public_rare_drop must bind the same committed eligible chest receipt; HG_DROP_MACAQUE_PUBLIC, HG_DROP_JIAO_PUBLIC, and HG_DROP_SHARK_PUBLIC must never use drop_bundle.

hash_contract.resource_table_file_hash: SHA-256 over the immutable UTF-8 resource-table file bytes, stored out-of-band in the decision register
hash_contract.award_plan_hash: SHA-256 lowercase hexadecimal over RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme UTF-8 bytes of the resolved award plan, including every grant, duplicate conversion, pity state transition, qualification snapshot identity, XP base/source-level/character-level/multiplier/session inputs and experience_delta, tower weekly counter before/after values, and table version

persistent_receipt_contract.encounter_identity_rule: encounter_instance_id is an authoritative unique lifecycle identity. It is required for every receipt type, including quest and experience grants; event_id need only be unique inside that encounter instance.
persistent_receipt_contract.replay_rule: The same semantic identity and fingerprint returns the original terminal committed or rejected receipt without another mutation. The same semantic identity with a different fingerprint, including a different resource_table_version, is a terminal receipt_identity_conflict.
persistent_receipt_contract.cross_version_origin_rule: A resource-table migration may create new receipts only for new authoritative events. The same origin identity may never be re-settled under a later resource_table_version; it is a terminal conflict rather than a recalculation.
persistent_receipt_contract.public_rare_participation_chest_binding_: A public_rare_drop receipt must bind participation_chest_receipt_id and participation_chest_receipt_fingerprint to one committed eligible participation_chest receipt with the same owner_id, event_id, encounter_instance_id, qualification_snapshot_id, and resource_table_version. team_raid_rare_drop must keep both participation-chest fields null. A chest result never by itself creates rare eligibility.
persistent_receipt_contract.team_raid_event_binding_rule: For team_raid_rare_drop, receipt.event_id equals completion_event_id and receipt.encounter_instance_id equals raid_instance_id from the TEAM_RAID_RARE_ELIGIBILITY_V1 snapshot; the receipt cannot substitute another team event or instance.
persistent_receipt_contract.zero_award_pity_rule: For balance_or_stack_cap_reached or weekly_token_cap_reached, a receipt with a non-null pity_pool_key must persist pity_before equal to pity_after. It may not increment, reset, or consume pity. A receipt with no pity_pool_key keeps both fields null.
persistent_receipt_contract.atomicity_rule: Currency, material, unique, first-clear, pity, XP repeat quota, tower weekly quota, receipt, and origin writes commit in one authoritative serializable transaction governed by transactional_resolution_contract. A crash or timeout reconciles by terminal receipt identity before any retry; it may not re-run a grant blindly.
persistent_receipt_contract.migration_rule: Migration is forward-only. Existing receipts retain their original resource_table_version and award result. An unknown or unmapped record enters an auditable isolation queue; no automatic deletion, recalculation, or pity reset is permitted.
persistent_receipt_contract.proof_rule: authority_proof_ref must resolve through the authoritative encounter/progress provider before a persistent receipt can commit; a non-empty opaque string alone is insufficient for production.
persistent_receipt_contract.functional_retention_rule: Keep a committed receipt available for reconciliation for the lifetime of its character state and through every migration that can reference it. Legal or account-deletion retention is owned by the future service data policy and may not weaken this functional reconciliation rule.

runtime_integration_gates: A future implementation must compile this table exactly and prove its content hash/version binding before it can set runtime_handoff=true.
The authoritative persistent store must enforce the receipt identity and fingerprint conflict rule across process restart and reconnect.
The encounter adapter must resolve authority_proof_ref and qualification snapshots; client or UI values are never evidence.
The existing implementation/growth f6h-v1 simulator remains a historical offline test fixture. It is not an economy-v1 runtime implementation and cannot be promoted by this document alone.
Y3 editor data, map root, object IDs, multiplayer synchronization, service storage, and live 30/60/90-minute balance validation remain separate production gates.
